newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss govt hopes to reach EU agreement by summer.
newsitem.headline: Swiss govt hopes to reach EU agreement by summer.

text.p: The Swiss government said Wednesday it still hopes to reach a major bilateral agreement with the European Union (EU) by summer.

"The Swiss cabinet today reemphasized its firm desire to bring the negotiations to a conclusion before the summer break," Swiss government spokesman Achille Casanova said in a statement after a cabinet meeting.

"In order to achieve this, it will hold intense discussions with Swiss Federal and Cantonal authorities, as well as with the governing political parties, and interest groups in areas of transport and ecology," Casanova said in a statement.

The bilateral agreement, once settled, is expected to provide a boost to the sluggish Swiss economy by improving trade and commercial ties with the EU countries. Negotiations hit a snag in late April due to differences over truck traffic.
The Swiss cabinet said it made a detailed study of matters where there are still differences, "especially in the areas of free movement of persons, as well as land and air transport."

A road transport deal, one of six issues in the planned agreement, bogged down when Switzerland and the EU found no compromise on road taxes for trucks, nor the weight of trucks to be allowed on fragile Swiss alpine roads.
They are also discussing how and whether 40-tonne EU lorries should be admitted onto Swiss roads. The Swiss currently ban lorries weighing more than 28 tonnes.
Switzerland, not one of the 15 EU members, holds the transport key for much of southern Europe.
Neighboring Austria especially is interested in resolving the transport pact.

There are also questions pertaining rules governing commercial airlines, including the right of an airline to carry traffic between two countries outside its home base, as well as regulations regarding cross-border movement of persons and related rights of foreigners to own Swiss property . -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
